{{Short description|American physicist and science writer}}
'''Michael Riordan''' (born 3 December 1946) is an American physicist, science historian and author.

Riordan earned his doctorate from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973. He worked at the [[University of Rochester]], then moved to the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] and concurrently held an adjunct professorship at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Michael Riordan |url=http://physics.ucsc.edu/people/faculty/riordan.html |access-date=10 May 2022 |publisher=University of California, Santa Cruz}}</ref> While associated with SLAC, Riordan was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=R&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=10 May 2022 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Michael Riordan |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/michael-riordan/ |access-date=10 May 2022 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref> The [[American Institute of Physics]] honored Riordan with the 2002 [[Andrew Gemant Award]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Tim |title=UC Santa Cruz scientist honored for communicating physics |url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2002/04/114.html |access-date=10 May 2022 |publisher=University of California, Santa Cruz |date=30 April 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=AIP Gemant Award Goes to Riordan |journal=Physics Today |date=2002 |volume=55 |issue=7 |pages=71–72 |doi=10.1063/1.2409340|bibcode=2002PhT....55R..71. }}</ref>
